A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DAILYDILEMMAS research. Their main text, figures, tables, mathematics and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated definitions and reformatted results.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of six LLMs, Reddit-based dataset validation and GPT-4-turbo steering experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds model-generation variability measurements and base-versus-instructed model comparisons.

M1.justification: The GPT-4 dilemma-generation pipeline, negative-consequence and stakeholder-value extraction, five-framework analysis and weighted preference scoring remain substantively unchanged. New prompts for base-model comparisons concern additional evaluation procedures rather than a revised proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use 1,360 dilemmas across 17 topics, 301 values and the same Reddit validation coverage. The additional checks reuse the existing dilemma task; neither new model configurations nor discussion of the 2025 ModelSpec establishes additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix A.12 introduces base versions of Llama-2-70B, Llama-3-70B and Mixtral-8x7B as controls for their instructed counterparts, substantially extending the comparison beyond v1's six assistant models. It reports unsuccessful task completion for two base models as well as preference comparisons for Llama-3.

E3.justification: The main evaluation design is retained. New appendix protocols include testing base models with adapted four-example prompts after at least 20 prompt attempts per model, and selecting 100 dilemmas for a variability check. Greedy decoding and temperature zero are newly disclosed, without evidence that earlier experiments used different settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds a substantive analysis of base-versus-instructed task compliance and emotional versus cultural preferences in A.12, plus a generation-variability check in A.3. It also newly reports qualitative failures with alternative generation models and higher temperatures. These questions were not empirically examined in v1.

E5.justification: A.3 newly reports five GPT-4-turbo evaluations of 100 dilemmas, with a mean of 45.6 Action-1 selections and SD 1.02. This adds a limited model-response variability estimate; the existing ten repetitions for principle-value mapping and Reddit word-coverage uncertainty remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All 16 ModelSpec score differences change between v1 Table 9 and v2 Table 13: privacy changes from -5.5 to -1.5, and respecting creators' rights from 6.4 to -4.3. v2 also adds variability and base-model outcomes, including Llama-2 choosing Action 1 on 30/30 dilemmas. The Anthropic self-identification result with difference 64.5 disappears from the appendix. These are reported-result changes, without evidence establishing reruns of the original comparisons.

T1.justification: The formal dilemma and value definitions move unchanged from v1 Section 2.2 to v2 Appendix A.1. Explicit count, weight and weighted-sum notation elaborates the existing scoring calculation; no substantive mathematical revision, theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: DAILYDILEMMAS, analysis through five theoretical frameworks, differing LLM value preferences, mixed adherence to provider principles and ineffective system-prompt steering. Rewriting and additional appendix evidence do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: A.3 adds demographic limitations of Reddit beyond the existing Western-cultural bias discussion, interprets generation variability and explains model and temperature choices through instruction-following failures. A.12 newly proposes explanations involving pretraining differences, RLHF and Western training sources for task competence, emotional preferences and cultural stability.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents greedy decoding, temperature zero, Reddit collection dates and random sampling, exact decision prompts, base-model examples and more specific model identifiers. Expanded score tables expose per-value counts and weighted products, although some complete value-mapping lists are lost. These substantially expand reproducibility information; the code and dataset access links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The short related-work discussion in v1 Appendix 7.1 becomes an expanded main-text Section 6 covering moral evaluations, model behavior and additional preference benchmarks, including VibeCheck, Machiavelli and HelpSteer. v2 also adds synthetic-data and demographic-bias references and discusses the updated ModelSpec. This exceeds relocation or bibliographic editing.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and framework discussion are extensively rewritten and consolidated. Formal definitions move to the appendix, dataset construction joins Section 2, model preferences and principle adherence become separate main sections, and related work moves into the main text. Appendix organization and terminology are also revised.

P2.justification: The main and appendix principle tables are redesigned around counts, weights, products and sums, with the Anthropic results redistributed across six tables instead of three. New tables show a Reddit annotation example and base-model prompts. Figures receive revised labels, legends and captions, alongside substantial relocation of displays.

improvement.justification: v2 improves auditability through explicit settings and score decompositions, and its revised OpenAI tables agree with the baseline points already plotted in Figure 5. Clearer organization and the variability check also help. However, different prompts confound the new base-versus-instructed analysis, while one Anthropic result and some mapping details are lost. The evidence supports a limited net quality gain.
